speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Significant rapid breathing. I also have Appears unwell, Diminished appetite, No fever, Swelling in the legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome. The combination of significant edema (legs and likely abdomen/face), rapid breathing due to ascites, diminished appetite, and absence of fever or respiratory infection signs in a 3-year-old is classic for this condition. The absence of dark urine or foaming in the history does not rule it out given the severity of the edema, and the metabolic panel should have already shown hypoalbuminemia and hyperlipidemia.
